NextAuth's own sign-in/callback/session/csrf endpoints (export const { GET, POST } = handlers — not detected by the export-function regex, so this file's methods here are hand-verified from src/lib/auth.js, not regex-extracted). Inherently must be reachable pre-session; creates/updates sessions and, on OAuth callback, User rows via the Prisma adapter. This is a 5th public+stateChanging route NOT in the Task 2 brief's enumerated exception list (stripe/webhook, webhooks/*, auth/register, contact) — flagged prominently in the task report for explicit sign-off. NextAuth has its own CSRF-token protection for the credentials flow, independent of this app's Task 3 origin-check work.

Public by design — Task 2 brief's enumerated public+stateChanging exception. Rate-limited by a custom in-memory per-IP counter (10 attempts/10min) local to this file, NOT the shared checkRateLimit/RATE_LIMITS map (rateLimit is 'none' here because the manifest's rateLimit field tracks checkRateLimit keys only). First-ever registered user is auto-promoted to admin (bootstrap) with no further gate. IP is read from X-Forwarded-For, trivially spoofable without a trusted reverse proxy in front.

ANOMALY: NOT requireAdminUser/role-based RBAC — uses a hardcoded 2-address DEV_EMAILS allowlist checked against the NextAuth session email via auth(), independent of the User.role column. A role='admin' DB user not in DEV_EMAILS is refused (403); conversely a DEV_EMAILS address whose DB role isn't 'admin' still passes. Also execs `pm2 logs` for helmies-app/helmies-bites/helmies-studio/all (cross-app log disclosure) gated only by that hardcoded list, with no rate limit. Recommend migrating to requireAdminUser in a follow-up.

Task 3 origin-check target. Creates a Stripe billing-portal session (external side effect, no local DB write). No rate limit.

GET is public (lists active CreditPack rows — price list only, no PII, no auth check). POST requires user auth, creates a Stripe Checkout Session and possibly a placeholder Subscription row; no rate limit — same Stripe-API-abuse anomaly as stripe/checkout. Task 3 origin-check target (POST only).

Public by design — Task 2 brief's enumerated public+stateChanging exception, and a Phase 1-2 fact ('signature-verified public'). Protected by Stripe signature verification (stripe-signature header + STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET via stripe.webhooks.constructEvent) — NOT the WEBHOOK_SECRET/CRON_SECRET bearer pattern used by /api/webhooks/* and /api/cron/*. Idempotent via a unique constraint on StripeEvent.stripeEventId claimed inside the same transaction as every credit grant. Not a Task 3 origin-check target — Stripe's servers call this directly, not a browser.

ANOMALY: GET with a side effect — unconditionally calls recordTemplateUse() on every successful call, decrementing usage against the caller's TemplatePurchase. Violates HTTP GET safety/idempotency and is reachable via a plain cookie-riding cross-site GET (e.g. an / tag) with no CSRF protection possible for a GET (Task 3's origin-check work targets state-changing requests broadly, but GET requests are typically exempted by convention — this route is exactly why that convention is dangerous here). Recommend converting to POST in a follow-up.
GET is public (template detail + optional personalized hasAccess via a best-effort auth() call). PUT/DELETE require requireAdmin. Task 3 origin-check target (PUT/DELETE only).

Task 3 origin-check target. Creates a Stripe Checkout Session (onetime pricing model) or a TemplatePurchase row (subscription-included model) per call; no rate limit — same Stripe-API-abuse anomaly noted on stripe/checkout et al.
